title: Lattice matching for epitaxy
summary: III-V semiconductors and their alloys by lattice constant and band gap: Vegard's law makes the lattice constant linear in composition, so a film can be tuned to fit its substrate.

concepts.label: III-V semiconductor
concepts.description: A compound of a group III metal (Al, Ga, In) and a group V element (N, P, As, Sb), zincblende here.

children.label: Lattice constant
children.description: Cubic cell edge, Å: from PBE (Alexandria) and measured (COD).

children.label: Semiconductor alloy
children.description: A mixed crystal such as In(x)Ga(1−x)As; here as ordered cells at x = 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4.

children.label: Vegard's law
children.description: The alloy's lattice constant is the composition-weighted mean of the end points.

children.label: Band-gap bowing
children.description: E(x) = (1−x)E0 + xE1 − b x(1−x); b from the alloys.

children.label: Random alloy
children.description: Real alloys have random cation order (special quasirandom structures model it), not the ordered cells computed here.

concepts.label: Epitaxy
concepts.description: Growing a crystalline film that continues the substrate's lattice (MBE, MOCVD).

children.label: Substrate
children.description: The wafer the film grows on: Si, GaAs, InP.

children.label: Lattice mismatch
children.description: (a_film − a_substrate)/a_substrate; matched composition x* where it is zero.

children.label: Critical thickness
children.description: The thickness above which a strained film relaxes by forming misfit dislocations (Matthews–Blakeslee); falls roughly as 1/mismatch.

facts.text: Matthews and Blakeslee, Defects in epitaxial multilayers, J. Cryst. Growth 27, 118 (1974).

concepts.label: Density functional theory
concepts.description: PBE: lattice constants 1–2% too large, gaps too small; the measured COD values check it.
